A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GIFT framework and experimental use cases. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original CLEVR rule-recovery experiments, CelebA causal concept measurements, and BDD-OIA bias-discovery evaluations in Section 4 and Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds CLEVR results with Qwen, caption-error audits, and a manual intervention-quality evaluation.

M1.justification: The four-stage procedure, DI prefilter, intervention-based verification, and optional manual concept combinations are retained. The added Qwen experiment tests another configuration of the existing framework without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CLEVR rule tasks, CelebA young/old classification, and biased BDD-OIA turn-right classification. The new audits examine these existing domains. Medical and multiclass applications are discussed but not experimentally added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the BDD-OIA comparison and CLEVR caption ablation is unchanged. Qwen is an additional GIFT configuration. The newly discussed methods and conceptual comparison in v3 Table 5 do not constitute additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds a Qwen2.5-72B CLEVR configuration and manual audit protocols: five counterfactual pairs per domain and 50 edited images per concept and operation. Figure 4 changes the stated BDD DI threshold from 15% to 5%; its unchanged results do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands component-reliability analysis through quantified caption errors on CelebA and BDD and manual editing-quality checks for three facial attributes, illustrated in Figures 9–10 and Table 8. It also tests another Stage 3 LLM. Existing stage ablations and counterfactual-count analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new audits provide counts and point percentages without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing causal-score tables and BDD results retain their values. Added Qwen results recover 11/12 CLEVR rules, missing purple-object/ResNet rather than GPT's red-metal-object/ResNet case. New diagnostic outcomes include 18/55 incorrect CelebA descriptions, 14/35 incorrect BDD descriptions, Table 8 intervention-quality percentages, and runtime measurements.

T1.justification: v3 explicitly assumes edited images remain in distribution and introduces a conditional-expectation definition of CaCE in Equation 2, creating ambiguity with its retained intervention-based estimator. The PNS derivation and CaCE–PNS identity proof otherwise match v2 Appendix A and v3 Appendix C.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion qualify faithfulness as supported by causal verification and explicitly restrict demonstrated applicability to binary classification and the tested image domains. The novelty statement now emphasizes global, textual, counterfactual explanations. The central rule-, concept-, and bias-discovery contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 extends the existing limitations discussion with specialized-domain requirements, editing failures and false negatives, confounding and precision–recall arguments, and multiclass computational scaling. Appendix G.2 additionally argues that nonsystematic editing side effects cannot influence causal inference, a stronger interpretation than its manual audit establishes.

D1.justification: Appendix I newly reports A100 hardware, batch sizes, and stage runtimes; most existing implementation details remain. v3 omits v2's explicit repository link and released-framework statement. Its runtime paragraph labels CelebA Stage 1 as OCTET, conflicting with the retained ACE implementation description.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of MAIA, Kuhn et al.'s shortcut mitigation, and newer attribution and surrogate work. Appendix B/Table 5 expands comparisons with TCAV, ACE, and CRAFT. Adebayo and Torfason citations are removed. The central counterfactual-based positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, related work, Stage 1 explanation, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Limitations move from Appendix G into main Section 5 and expand; the impact statement moves into Appendix A. New related-work and computational-footprint appendices further reorganize the document.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with extensively rearranged tables and captions. Table 2 gains a Qwen column; Tables 5 and 8 and Figures 9–10 are added. The original main-text BDD intervention Figure 5 moves to appendix Figure 16.

improvement.justification: The new component audits, additional LLM evaluation, runtime disclosure, and clearer applicability limits make reliability more assessable than in v2. The overall gain is limited: caption audits are small, the dismissal of editing confounding is unsupported, the new CaCE equation blurs conditioning with intervention, and explicit repository access information is lost. These issues prevent the added evidence from establishing a substantial improvement in causal validation.
